findings.question: Q4
findings.title: A handed, not-read-back state shorter than a history another in-flight verification already accepted is never recorded and never compared: a longer restore-plus-charges state that rewrote it is accepted, and the executed action is admitted and dispatched again (the outcome depends on which verification compares first)
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:647-660 `_note_unread`: when no unread state is recorded yet (`earlier is None`), the state's entry objects are recorded only `if len(entries) >= len(self._seen.get(key, ()))`. A shorter state is assumed to be 'behind' (docstring line 649: 'a shorter one is behind it'), but nothing checks that it is a prefix of what was seen: `_seen` holds content digests, not entry objects, and the unread state's content was never read. The comparison (lines 714-721) and the post-wait recheck (746-755) only look at `_unread_entries`, so a state that was never recorded can never refuse anything. Probe C:\Users\DEV_KA~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-dev-kaeem-Downloads-Compressed-phyx\b5e3066d-77b7-465b-b1bf-cfd7098cdf27\scratchpad\r14\C-adversarial-bypass\p1.sh (WSL ~/br11-review/r14/C-adversarial-bypass/p1_order.py), run against ~/forge-r14-review at 1c9fdd84. Output for 'concurrent': `V1: refused: ... was not read back ...`, `V2 (fresh world from the owners): DISPATCHED AGAIN`, `executor calls: 2  unread entries: {}  diverged: []`. Output for 'sequential' (the same steps, with V1 comparing first): `V2: projection refused: ... rewrote the entries of a state of it a verification was handed and could not read back`, `executor calls: 1`, diverged. The same result comes through the Mind-facing MindWorldPort.request_admission + execute (p2.sh / p2_port_order.py): `port re-admission: DISPATCHED AGAIN | executor calls: 2`, and the charge ids afterwards are ['...spent', 'other.1', 'other.2', 'run.2'], so run.1's spend is gone.
findings.reproduction: Use the repository's own harness (benchmarks fixtures ax.owned('battery'), BudgetReader.following(lambda: (dict(o.ledgers), dict(o.experiments))), ExecutionDesk(...).gateway()). (1) Dispatch simulate_pulse. The executor settles run.1 whose detail's __str__ raises the interpreter's own 'dictionary changed size during iteration' (the code itself classifies this as an honest concurrent move, so the account is 'not read back'), slowly (0.2 s per attempt) on thread V1. (2) Thread V1 starts a verification and is handed S1 = S0+run.1. (3) While V1 is still reading back, the execution side does a checkpoint restore by object replacement (o.ledgers[lid] = BudgetLedger.from_dict(s0.to_dict()), the sria.campaign pattern) and settles two other charges (n0+2 entries). (4) The main thread projects a fresh world and admits and dispatches simulate_pulse. V2 reads back S0+o1+o2, accepts it and waits for V1. V1 compares within WAIT_S, but S1's n0+1 entries are fewer than n0+2, so they are not recorded. V2 decides, admission passes, and the executor runs a second time.
findings.why: This is the F13-02 outcome class again: a spend in a state handed to a verification and not read back is lost, a restore then re-authorizes it, and the action that spent it is dispatched again. It is reproduced through the shipped API with a normal restore and normal settles. None of the accepted residuals covers it. V1 was handed S1, V1 compared within WAIT_S, and V1 did not leave. The round-13 fix claims that 'a state handed and NOT read back is still observed as the entries of its history' and that 'a verification decides on an account only once every other verification in flight ... has compared too, whichever started first'. Here the decision depends on comparison order: the same states and the same verifications give refused-for-good in one order and a duplicate dispatch in the other. This is an unobserved spend that permits duplicate dispatch, so it is MAJOR under the brief, and Q4 is YES.
findings.fix: Keep the entry objects of the last accepted state per account (for example `_seen_entries[key] = before` when a history is recorded). In `_note_unread`, a shorter unread state must be an identity prefix of those entries (`_extends(seen_entries, entries)`); otherwise it rewrote the history and goes into `_diverged`. Alternatively, record every unread state's entries whatever their length and refuse any later accepted state that is neither an extension nor a prefix of them. Add a two-thread control that pins both comparison orders to the same refusal.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: The entries listed before a read-back ('before') are never compared with the state the read-back actually read: a state rewritten in place during its own read-back (between the listing and a later successful attempt) is accepted, and the listed state is dropped
findings.evidence: owners.py:604-607: `before = self._entries(key)`, then `record, history = self._account(key)` (up to three attempts), and `out[key] = (record, history, before)`. In `_observe_all` (699-728), `before` is used only to compare against a previously recorded unread state (`_extends(before, unread)`). It is never checked against `history`, and nothing lists the entries again after the read-back. Probe p2.sh / p3_inplace_during_readback.py: `handed S1 charge ids: ['...spent', 'run.1']`, `V1 served revision 2 charge ids now: ['...spent', 'other.1'] diverged: [] unread: {}`, `re-admission: DISPATCHED AGAIN | executor calls: 2`.
findings.reproduction: run.1's detail __str__ fires on attempt 1 of the next verification's read-back. It rewrites the handed ledger in place (object.__setattr__(led, 'charges', s0.charges + (other.1,))) and raises the mutation error. Attempt 2 reads S0+other.1 back (same length), and it extends the seen history S0 and is accepted. A fresh admission then dispatches simulate_pulse again.
findings.why: The reader listed S1's entries and then accepted a state that does not begin with them. That contradicts the stated invariant that a handed state not read back is observed by its entries. I rate it MINOR, not MAJOR, because the in-place rollback must bypass the owner's own BudgetHistoryViolation guard (object.__setattr__) or the experiment's private _evaluations list, and a rollback between two verifications already gives the same outcome (an accepted residual). It still makes Q4 PARTIAL on its own, but Q4 is already YES because of R14-C-F1.
findings.fix: List the entries again after a successful read-back. If they are not identical to `before` (identity and length), or the read-back history's length differs from `len(before)`, treat the account as moved: not read back, with `before` recorded via _note_unread.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Deterministic account content that raises GeneratorExit or SystemExit is treated as an interrupt: it is re-raised out of every admission, including ones on worlds that never read that account, and out of the following() constructor
findings.evidence: owners.py:124 `_INTERRUPTS = (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, GeneratorExit)`; 500-502 `_read_once` re-raises them; 612-615 and 756-757 the read-back records them and `_observe_all` re-raises after comparing. Every verification pins every reader (Authorities.memoized), so any admission raises. The docstring at 376-379 says 'an account is refused only to a verification that reads it, so an account no world reads refuses nothing'. Probe p5.sh / p5_content_interrupt.py: `GeneratorExit constructor raised GeneratorExit`, then `admission 0/1/2 RAISED GeneratorExit (world does not read side.ledger)`, and the same for SystemExit.
findings.reproduction: Settle a charge on a side ledger that no world reads, with a detail whose __str__ raises GeneratorExit (or SystemExit). Build BudgetReader.following over the solver ledgers plus that side ledger, then call admit() on the battery world three times. Each call raises instead of admitting.
findings.why: This is fail-closed: nothing is admitted and the spend is noted as unread entries, so it is not a bypass. But a property of an account's content, which is not an interrupt of the caller, permanently aborts every admission of the desk and contradicts the documented scope. It is the R13-C-F2 / F13-03 outcome class, narrowed to the three interrupt types. Rated MINOR as availability plus documentation.
findings.fix: Treat an interrupt-class exception raised from inside account content (the read-back's own call frames) as a classified failure, re-raising only interrupts delivered asynchronously. Or at least scope the re-raise so that a world that does not read the account still decides, and document that content raising SystemExit/GeneratorExit aborts every verification.

findings.question: Q4

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: A handed state that is not read back and is SHORTER than the observed history leaves no trace at all (not even its entry objects): a rewind-and-spend that is never read back, followed by a restore of the observed state, re-admits and re-dispatches the executed action, contrary to README section 4 and the class docstring
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:647-660 `_note_unread`: when no unread state is recorded yet (`earlier is None`, line 652), the entries are recorded only `if len(entries) >= len(self._seen.get(key, ()))` (line 653); otherwise nothing is recorded and None is returned, so `_observe_all` (owners.py:696-698) stores only the per-verification reason `got.why`. The justification in the docstring at owners.py:648-649, '(a shorter one is behind it)', is false: `_seen` holds content hashes (owners.py:458-460, 713), and a shorter state may be a REWRITE (for example `(c1', s)` against an observed `[c1, c2, c3]`), which a successful read-back would refuse for good at owners.py:704-709. A later readable state equal in content to the observed history then passes every check: history equal to `_seen` (owners.py:703-712), `_unread_entries` empty (owners.py:714-722), so it is accepted and served (owners.py:727-728). The report states the rule with no length condition: README.md:191-201 ('A state handed and NOT read back is still observed as the entries of its history ... A later state of that account is decided on only if its container begins with exactly those entry objects ... no later state that does not extend it is decided on'), README.md:222-223 ('a return to an earlier state never re-authorizes what such a state had moved past'), and owners.py:403-410 (class docstring, same claim). The NOT-pre-accepted item 'the content of a state handed and not read back is not observed (only its entry objects)' does not cover this: here even the entry objects are not kept. No control covers it: tests/mind/test_authority_review_r13.py:65-86 (F13-02) uses a state longer than the observed history, and :284-307 (R13-CRIT-2) only covers a shorter state after a longer one was recorded.
findings.reproduction: Static reading (lens E does not execute). Steps a skeptic can run against ~/forge-r14-review, using the same shape as test_authority_review_r13.py::test_a_spend_not_read_back_is_never_readmitted_after_a_restore_and_another_charge. (1) Battery fixture with a following BudgetReader over (dict(o.ledgers), dict(o.experiments)). Settle two honest charges c1 and c2 on the solver ledger, then read through the reader so that `_seen` has length 2. (2) Admit simulate_pulse; X is now bound to the digest of [c1, c2]. (3) The executor does what a checkpoint-rewinding campaign does: `o.ledgers[lid] = BudgetLedger.from_dict(<the empty-ledger checkpoint>)`, then `settle(charge_id='run.1', ..., detail=_SelfFillingNote())`, so the ledger is now [s]: length 1, shorter than 2, and never read back (the interpreter's mutation error on every attempt). (4) `reader.read(BUDGET_LEDGER, lid)` raises OwnerUnavailable 'not read back'; `reader._unread_entries` stays empty because `_note_unread` skipped it at line 653. (5) Restore the latest checkpoint: `o.ledgers[lid] = BudgetLedger.from_dict(<the [c1, c2] state>)`. (6) `gateway.dispatch(X)` re-admits: the history equals `_seen`, nothing unread is recorded, and the digest is identical, so the executor runs a second time. A successful read-back at step 4 would have refused the account for good (rewrote). Expected at HEAD: executor ran 2.
findings.why: The budget follower's forward-only guarantee for HANDED states is meant to ensure that a spend which was handed to a verification cannot be re-authorized by a later return to an earlier state. This finding is an unobserved handed spend that permits a duplicate dispatch: the MAJOR class of R10-C-F1, R11-C-F1, F11-2, R12-3 and F13-02. It is not inside the documented residual 'a state no verification was handed', because this state was handed and its entries were listed and then discarded by rule. The report and the docstring state the guarantee unconditionally, which overstates what is controlled. The trigger is the execution side's own checkpoint rewind before a charge, plus content that cannot be read back. That trigger is exotic, but the brief says not to downgrade for an exotic trigger, and F13-02 had the same unreadable-content trigger.
findings.fix: Record the entry objects of EVERY state handed and not read back when none is recorded, with no length precondition (owners.py:653). Alternatively, refuse the account for good when a not-read-back state is shorter than the observed history, since such a state is either a replacement or a rewrite and the two cannot be told apart without reading it. This gives the same fail-closed availability cost already documented for an object-replacing restore after an unread state. Correct the docstring at owners.py:648-649 and README section 4 to match. Add a failing-first control (the steps above: executor ran exactly 1), plus a mutant that restores the length precondition.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: Interrupt-class exceptions raised deterministically by account CONTENT are classified by type as interrupts: every admission and dispatch through the desk escapes with them (including worlds that never read the account), and every account read after it becomes 'not read back' at every verification
findings.evidence: Classification is by type, which the content chooses: owners.py:124 `_INTERRUPTS = (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, GeneratorExit)`, :127-128, :500-502 (re-raised from `_read_once`), :612-615 (`_read_back` keeps it), :756-757 (re-raised after the comparison). authority.py:383-387: `_Memo._pin_now` catches only `Exception`, so the re-raised interrupt leaves `Authorities.memoized()` at the start of every verification, whichever world is verified. After it, every later account in iteration order is recorded as not read back (owners.py:600-603 -> :618-623 -> :653-656). An honest object-replacing checkpoint restore of any of those accounts is then refused for good (owners.py:715-720). This contradicts README.md:239-240 and owners.py:378-379 ('an account no world reads refuses nothing'). The builder's own 'Failed approach' note in PROGRESS (docs/work/PROGRESS.md:8975-8977) says that classifying by a failure's type 'cannot be made safe: an execution-side value chooses all three'. The round-13 control tests/mind/test_authority_review_r13.py:176-198 deliberately puts a KeyboardInterrupt subclass in a charge's detail and expects it to escape `pinned()`, so this is by design and no control tests it against an unbound account.
findings.reproduction: Static reading. Hand an unbound side ledger whose charge detail's `__str__` raises a `KeyboardInterrupt` subclass, as in test_an_account_raising_a_base_exception_no_world_reads_refuses_no_admission at test_authority_review_r13.py:166-173, but with `_Interrupt` instead of `_Halt`. Expected: `admit(...)` raises `_Interrupt` at every call instead of returning FEASIBLE, and accounts listed after the side ledger are recorded in `_unread_entries` at every verification.
findings.why: The spend is recorded (its entries), so there is no duplicate dispatch, and dispatch fails closed because the executor is never reached. However, a deterministic property of a handed state that no world reads stops every admission from returning a refusal record, and it can permanently retire honest accounts that are later restored by object replacement. This is availability and a semantic misstatement of a documented guarantee, not an authority leak.
findings.fix: Either treat an interrupt-class exception raised from inside account content the same way on every attempt (the same failure on the same text is the state itself: classify it as `_Unreadable`), or state the residual explicitly in README section 4. Do not record the not-yet-read accounts' entries after a reader-side interruption, or document that cost. Make `_Memo._pin_now` keep a non-Exception raised by a pin until a read of that owner, or document why it does not.

findings.question: Q4
findings.title: The round-13 guarantee of one fresh read-back thread per account is not held when verifications run concurrently: the check and the registration are not atomic
findings.evidence: src/engcore/mind/world/owners.py:553-573 reads `earlier = self._fresh.get(key)` and checks `earlier.is_alive()`, then builds and starts the thread, and only then runs `self._fresh[key] = thread`. No lock is held anywhere in that sequence, and `_fresh` is shared across verifications (owners.py:845). The docstrings at owners.py:412-413 and 551-552 and README.md:207-208 say that while one fresh thread runs, no other verification starts a second one for the same account. Probe C:\Users\DEV_KA~1\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-dev-kaeem-Downloads-Compressed-phyx\b5e3066d-77b7-465b-b1bf-cfd7098cdf27\scratchpad\r14\B-architecture\p01_probes.py, section P2 (output in ~/br11-review/r14/B-architecture/p01_probes.out): 'trials with two fresh read-back threads alive for one account at once: 24/30'. Run sequentially (section P3), 6 verifications leave exactly 1 thread alive, so the sequential claim holds. The round-13 control test_a_blocked_fresh_thread_is_not_joined_by_another_for_the_same_account starts its verifications one after another, so the concurrent case has no control.
findings.reproduction: cd ~/forge-r14-review && PYTHONPATH=$HOME/forge-r14-review/src:$HOME/forge-r14-review ~/forge-gen2-authority-v1/.venv/bin/python ~/br11-review/r14/B-architecture/p01_probes.py (P2). Setup: one ledger whose charge detail's __str__ raises RecursionError on verifier threads, meeting at a 2-party barrier on the third attempt, and blocks on the 'budget-read-back' thread. Two threads call reader.pinned() at the same time, with BudgetReader.WAIT_S set to 0.3 in the probe process.
findings.why: This is a correctness defect in an invariant the round-13 fix claims to have closed (E13-F5 / R13-C-F4 / R13-A-F4 / R13-B-F4). Its effect is limited to resources: each concurrent verification can start one extra blocked daemon thread per account, the overwritten thread is no longer tracked, and the count is bounded by concurrency in each generation. No budget decision, admission or dispatch changes, because each thread fills only its own private cache and result box. Under the reporting convention, a resource-only effect does not by itself make Q4 PARTIAL.
findings.fix: Do the check and the registration under the reader's lock: no execution-side code runs between them, and Thread.start may stay outside if a placeholder is registered first. Or reword owners.py:412-413, 551-552 and README:207-208 to 'per verification thread, not across concurrent verifications'. Add a concurrent control.

findings.reproduction: Use the battery fixture with BudgetReader.following(accounts). accounts() returns dict(o.ledgers) until the executor settles run.1 on the solver ledger, then returns types.MappingProxyType(dict(o.ledgers)) (or an honest Mapping class). gateway.dispatch(r.admitted) runs the executor. reader.read(BUDGET_LEDGER, solver) is refused with 'no pair of account mappings', and nothing is recorded. Then restore: o.ledgers[solver] = BudgetLedger.from_dict(<pre-spend to_dict>), and accounts() returns a plain dict again. gateway.dispatch(r.admitted) now succeeds and the executor runs a second time. Run: wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- bash -s < .../scratchpad/r14/critic/p2.sh
findings.why: Q4's forward-only guarantee rules out an unobserved spend that leads to duplicate dispatch. Here an executed action's spend was handed to a verification and then dropped whole, and the same authorization executes twice. This behaviour is new in 13051154 and is NOT pre-accepted: the task lists 'a handed mapping that is not a dict is refused to that verification and its state not observed' as a new behaviour to judge. The owner accepted 'accounts() raises or hands no pair of mappings' when an honest Mapping was still read (dict(mapping)). At 3b407ddb an honest Mapping or MappingProxyType spend was observed and refused (demonstrated above), so 13051154 widened that residual by redefining what a mapping is. The API annotation still invites a Mapping, and MappingProxyType is FORGE's usual read-only idiom (engcore/domains/__init__.py:134, engcore/execution/trusted.py:98, engcore/design/*). B-F4 judged this behaviour 'fail closed' and F14-F6 reported only the annotation mismatch; neither ran the outcome. The refusal only applies to the one verification, and the unobserved state is exactly what lets the duplicate dispatch through. Rounds 10, 11 and 13 showed this pattern: the newest change introduced a MAJOR in the budget follower.
findings.fix: Treat a handed value the reader cannot read as a state that may hold a spend. Either refuse every account of that reader for good once accounts() hands a non-dict (a new timeline needs a new reader), or record a reader-wide 'unobserved handed state' marker that refuses any later state until the execution side states a new reader. Also change the following() annotation (and the constructor's) to dict. Add a control that asserts the outcome, not only the refusal: after a MappingProxyType spend and a restore, the same authorization is refused and the executor runs once.

findings.evidence: tests/mind/test_authority_review_r13.py:251-272 (test_a_handed_mapping_that_is_not_a_dict_refuses_the_verification asserts only pytest.raises(OwnerUnavailable, match='no pair of account mappings'); it passes at 1c9fdd84 although the same authorization is re-dispatched, see CRIT14-1). tests/mind/test_authority_review_r13.py:284-307 (R13-CRIT-2) covers an unread state shorter than an earlier UNREAD state, never one shorter than _seen. owners.py:651-654: `if earlier is None: if len(entries) >= len(self._seen.get(key, ())): self._unread_entries[key] = entries`, with no else branch, is the root cause of R14-A-F1/R14-C-F1/D14-F1/F14-F1/E14-F1. docs/work/evidence/br11_local_2026_10_23/round13/mutation/mutate_r13_local.py and summary_first_pass.txt list no mutant for this branch, and all 685 tests pass (D-replay-stale/suite.out; round13/checks/suite.txt).

findings.why: A guarantee whose only control checks that a refusal text appears can regress to unobserved spend without any test failing, which is exactly what CRIT14-1 shows. The not-read-back floor that drops shorter states has no control at all. This is a test-coverage gap with no wrong outcome of its own, so it is MINOR, but it is the reason both MAJORs got through a green suite and a 'killed' mutation pass.
findings.fix: For every 'refused to this verification, state not observed' path, add outcome controls in the style of _readmitted/_refused: after the unobserved spend and a restore, a fresh world is refused and the same authorization is refused. Add a control for a not-read-back state shorter than _seen followed by a restore of the observed checkpoint. Add mutants for the owners.py:653 floor and for the _items refusal path.

B-F4 called the not-a-dict behaviour 'fail closed', which CRIT14-1 disproves.
